sample_unit: surgical video frames (from 3 procedures) rated by 6 surgeons
models_evaluated: convolutional neural network real-time fluorescence-like navigation (FLN) prostatic capsule segmentation model

links.outcome: Segmentation performance (Dice) under visual interference and distant-view surgical scenarios
links.effect: Mean Dice was 0.622 in Phase I, 0.489 in Phase II (bleeding/smoke), 0.616 in Phase III and 0.390 in Phase IV (distant view); overall Dice 0.533 ± 0.098.
links.quote: Performance varied across surgical scenarios with mean Dice scores of 0.622 in Phase I, 0.489 in Phase II, 0.616 in Phase III, and 0.390 in Phase IV, yet surgeon reliability ratings remained high across all phases (8.39-9.10/10).

links.outcome: Correlation between objective segmentation accuracy and surgeon acceptance ratings, indicating whether users detect weaker AI outputs
links.effect: Surgeon ratings stayed high (8.21-9.01/10) despite moderate Dice (0.533); Dice-rating correlation was weak (r = 0.42, p = 0.048). Authors interpret this as well-calibrated trust.
links.quote: Weak positive correlation between Dice scores and clinical ratings was observed (r = 0.42, p = 0.048).

unlisted_practices: Human-in-the-loop expert surgeon rating of real-time AI intraoperative navigation output on structured clinical domains
Tuning AI toward high recall over precision for surgical safety

screen.reason: The study conducts an offline reader validation and clinical acceptance assessment of an intraoperative surgical video AI segmentation model by 6 urologic surgeons across diverse clinical scenarios, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
